page: Microsoft Azure F72s_v2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 72 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 36 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture and includes 144.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a bundled 590 GB drive, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 67087.24 and a PassMark CPU score of 50595.14, both placing in the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, registering strong uncached read speeds of 206.9 GB/sec and write speeds of 95.3 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core performance of 1454.7 and Geekbench single-core score of 1252.0, fall into the average category. Large-model LLM text generation represents a performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F72s_v2 offers high compute density with its 72 dedicated vCPUs, making it highly resource-efficient for parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory-to-CPU ratios. The combination of high multi-core throughput and moderate memory capacity makes this server type suitable for compute-heavy tasks such as ray tracing, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and high-throughput web serving. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM text generation.
